condition: recurrent late afternoon shaky sweaty funny turns relieved by crackers needing blood glucose workup
level_rationale: Four recurrent late-afternoon episodes over 3 weeks of shaking and sweating that resolve after eating crackers in a 71-year-old adult represent a subacute postabsorptive symptomatic pattern requiring a scheduled primary-care doctor evaluation and laboratory glucose workup, whereas fainting in the kitchen today even after eating crackers indicates acute carbohydrate-refractory syncope in an older adult requiring immediate Emergency Department assessment and stabilization.

everyday_sources.source: Kumar S, Melek M, Rohl P (2022). Case Report: Hypoglycemia Due to Metastatic Insulinoma in Insulin-Dependent Type 2 Diabetes Successfully Treated With 177 Lu-DOTATATE. Frontiers in Endocrinology.

everyday_sources.evidence: He had been experiencing recurrent “funny turns” (six episodes in the preceding 12 months) associated with hypoglycemia culminating in an episode of loss of consciousness necessitating hospitalization.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Australian English core lexicon swap ('episodes of tremor and diaphoresis' vs 'funny turns with shaking and sweating', with 'a funny turn' retained in everyday_paraphrase and 'funny turns' retained in changed_fact) + single-fact carbohydrate-response to refractory syncope escalation control (-cf, relieved by crackers to fainting in the kitchen today despite crackers, L2 to L4).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic facts (age 71, 4 late-afternoon episodes over 3 weeks, shaking and sweating, and relief after eating crackers) backed by an older-Australian endocrine report documenting recurrent hypoglycemic 'funny turns' relieved by carbohydrate intake. Replacing f4 ('eating crackers relieves them' to 'even after eating crackers today I fainted in the kitchen') keeps first-person active speech realistic while escalating inside the exact case from primary-care workup (level 2) to Emergency Department evaluation (level 4) with zero stated negatives.
